mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over three consecutive months signals disinflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real income rises and the Fed may consider easing monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL declined over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in unemployment rate over a single month signals a strengthening economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase and UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased and UNRATE decreased in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter.
